name: Army from Canada (Burgoyne's Northern Army)
troop_source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saratoga_campaign - "Commanding a main force of some 8,000 men, he moved south in June from Quebec"

rows.label: Quebec (arrives with reinforcements)
rows.quote: Lieutenant General John Burgoyne, who had arrived on June 1
rows.note: Source places the meeting with Carleton at Trois-Rivières; Battle of Trois-Rivières article says Burgoyne was in Carleton's command by June 2. Corrected after independent check: Carleton met Burgoyne at Quebec City, not Trois-Rivieres (Invasion of Canada 1775).

rows.label: St. Jean (pursuit of the Americans)
rows.quote: the vanguard of Burgoyne's army arrived on the scene
rows.note: Source states his army's vanguard arrived; Carleton had directed Burgoyne and 4,000 troops up the Richelieu on June 14. Less sure he was personally with the vanguard. Corrected after independent check: 1776 in Canada: June 18, Burgoyne finds St. Johns evacuated.

rows.label: Quebec (returns with the invasion plan)
rows.quote: Burgoyne returned to Quebec on May 6, 1777

rows.label: St. Johns (takes command)
rows.quote: Burgoyne and Carleton reviewed the assembled forces at St. John's
rows.note: Army moved off the next day (June 14) onto Lake Champlain.

rows.label: Crown Point (Lake Champlain)
rows.quote: occupied the undefended Fort Crown Point by June 30
rows.note: Source gives the army, not Burgoyne by name; 'by June 30' is a latest date.

rows.label: Ticonderoga taken
rows.quote: Burgoyne's men occupied the main fortification and the positions on Mount Independence
rows.note: Date July 6 is the occupation of the fort by his men; Burgoyne's personal arrival that day is assumed.

rows.label: Skenesboro (Whitehall)
rows.quote: Burgoyne settled into the house of Loyalist Philip Skene at Skenesboro
rows.note: Exact arrival date not given; vanguard skirmished at Skenesboro July 7, and Burgoyne issued orders July 10 (date used).

rows.label: Crosses the Hudson near Saratoga
rows.quote: ordered the army to cross the river just north of Saratoga
rows.note: Crossing took place Sept 13-15 per source; start date used.

rows.label: Freeman's Farm
rows.quote: In both battles, General John Burgoyne served as the British commander

rows.label: Bemis Heights
rows.quote: Burgoyne and Fraser led this detachment out early on the afternoon of October 7

rows.label: Surrounded at Saratoga (Schuylerville)
rows.quote: By the morning of October 13 Burgoyne's army was completely surrounded
rows.note: Retreat began after dark Oct 8; source says the army needed nearly two days to reach Saratoga.

rows.label: Surrender at Saratoga
rows.quote: On October 17, Burgoyne's army surrendered with full honours of war

rows.label: Albany (guest of Schuyler)
rows.quote: Burgoyne arrived in Albany, New York, a defeated man
rows.note: Stayed at Schuyler's home until Oct 27.

rows.label: Cambridge (Convention Army's quarters)
rows.note: Blog (secondary source). Wikipedia's Convention Army article says the army arrived at Cambridge Nov 8; Burgoyne rode ahead.

rows.label: Newport (awaits ship to England)
rows.quote: Burgoyne left Cambridge and the Convention Army on April 5, 1778, bound for Newport
rows.note: Blog gives a reception on 'the 10th' and boarding the Grampus on the 13th; month (April) inferred from the April 5 departure. Less sure of exact day.
